name: Alaska
exemptPretaxComment: Not applicable -- no income tax exists for any pretax category to reduce the base of. Added for schema consistency with this project's other no-income-tax states (comprehensive-audit pass).

reciprocity.note: Not applicable -- Alaska has no income tax to be reciprocal about, same convention as this project's other no-income-tax states. Added for schema consistency (comprehensive-audit pass) -- this field was previously missing entirely from this file, unlike every other no-income-tax state's file.

sources.title: Alaska Dept of Labor and Workforce Development, Employment Security Tax -- 2026 Unemployment Insurance Tax Rates
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly. Quoted verbatim: 'The 2026 Taxable Wage Base is $54,200.00' and 'The 2026 Employee Rate is 0.50%.' The full 21-class variable-contribution-rate table was also read: the EMPLOYER rate is experience-rated (1.00% to 5.40% across the 21 classes), but the EMPLOYEE rate is a flat 0.50% for every single class with no exceptions -- Alaska's employee-paid UI share is genuinely NOT experience-rated at all, unlike the employer side of the same tax.

sources.title: Alaska Statutes 23.20 -- Alaska Employment Security Act (reciprocity/local tax context)
sources.verifiedBy: Search-synthesized (WebSearch, not independently fetched this pass): Alaska has no personal income tax of any kind (never has, since 1980) and no local municipal income/wage tax (municipalities may levy local sales taxes and specific excise taxes, e.g. a 'raw fish tax', but not a payroll/income tax). Alaska has no mandatory paid family/medical leave program -- a 2023-2024 HB 100 proposal was not enacted. The Alaska Family Leave Act (AFLA, 50+ employees) provides only UNPAID job-protected leave, not a payroll deduction.

stateUnemploymentEmployee.$comment: Wired via the existing generic stateUnemploymentEmployeeTax() mechanism (already used for PA/NJ) -- zero new code. Alaska is one of only three states in this project (with PA and NJ) that taxes the EMPLOYEE for unemployment insurance, not just the employer. Flat 0.50% for every employer regardless of the employer's own experience-rated class -- confirmed directly from the full 21-class rate table, not just the headline figure.

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE. No Alaska municipality or borough levies a local income/wage tax.
localIncomeTax.confidence: cross_source_confirmed; not independently verified against a specific municipal-authority statute this pass.

paidFamilyMedicalLeave.rule: NONE mandatory. The Alaska Family Leave Act (50+ employees) provides only unpaid, job-protected leave -- not a payroll deduction. A 2023-2024 legislative proposal (HB 100) to create a paid program was not enacted.
paidFamilyMedicalLeave.confidence: cross_source_confirmed via search synthesis, not independently fetched from a specific enacted statute this pass.

unemploymentInsuranceEmployer.administeredBy: Alaska Dept of Labor and Workforce Development
unemploymentInsuranceEmployer.delinquentOrIneligibleRateNote: Rate class 21 (the top negative-reserve class) carries an employer rate of 5.40%, total (with the flat 0.50% employee share) 5.90% -- the ceiling for any single employer.
unemploymentInsuranceEmployer.confidence: primary_source_confirmed -- labor.alaska.gov's own 2026 rate table, quoted directly above.
unemploymentInsuranceEmployer.knownGap: The employer side is experience-rated (21 classes by cumulative reportable payroll); stateUnemploymentEmployerTax() (src/taxes/state.ts) uses the caller-supplied rate when given (input.employer.stateUnemploymentRate) since this engine doesn't track an employer's own payroll history, otherwise the new-employer rate below. The EMPLOYEE side (flat 0.50%, no experience-rating) needs no such input. STILL OPEN: whether this state's unemployment wage base excludes the same pretax categories as its income tax withholding (the engine currently applies exemptPretax to both) — elective deferrals are commonly included in the unemployment base while excluded from income tax.
